prompt:
Paint ONE finished frame of a film-like cutscene of our hand-painted point-and-click adventure game 'Posledny zvonec' (Slovakia; eras 1960, 1982, 1995, 2020, 2035). The reference images are numbered in the order they are given: Image 1: place reference: the side path, the window and the garden (room S06 of our game) Image 2: character reference: grandmother Mira, 80 Image 3: character reference: our hero Adam (front and side view)

Shot: Wide calm shot of the house wall with the three windows and the garden beyond the green fence. Adam sits on a simple wooden bench placed against the wall below the big closed window, outside, relaxed for the first time, his bag beside him. Inside, behind the glass, Mira sits on a chair close to the window, facing him through the glass. Both hold their phones in their laps. The glass remains between them. Autumn garden, the vine with grapes, the tree in golden leaves.

Characters in this frame (briefs of the approved designs): Adam, a 35-year-old Slovak man who repairs audio equipment for a living: an ordinary, likeable civilian with a dry sense of humour. Short dark brown hair, clean-shaven with a hint of stubble, friendly slightly tired face, medium build, average height. He wears an open mid-blue cotton work jacket with chest pockets and the sleeves pushed up a little, a plain mustard-yellow T-shirt underneath, dark grey-blue jeans, and sturdy brown leather shoes. A brown leather messenger bag hangs on a strap across his chest and rests on his left hip. No hat, no coat, no tie, no uniform, no badge. Mira, Adam's 80-year-old grandmother, a retired engineer at home in her house in autumn 2020: sharp-eyed, precise, quietly tender, healthy and lively (not ill, not frail). Short white hair set in soft neat waves, round thin metal-framed glasses, an alert, wry, intelligent face with fine wrinkles and a small knowing smile. She wears a warm ochre (golden yellow-brown) knitted wool sweater over a white blouse collar, dark brown trousers and comfortable house shoes. She is indoors at home, so she wears no face mask. With her right hand she holds a plain dark mobile phone (no logo) to her right ear, the phone on the far side of her head so her whole face stays visible; her left arm is relaxed.

Light and time: Late golden hour turning to dusk, a warm lamp lit inside the room.

Character references show approved characters of the game on a plain grey card: copy each person's face, age, hair, body proportions, clothes and colours exactly, but pose and light them for this scene; never copy the grey card, the sheet layout or a duplicate of the same person. Place references show the real location and its painted version in our game: keep its architecture, materials and era. Photos are only references: repaint everything in our style, paint any real people in them out, and do not copy brand logos or shop names. Composition: a cinematic 16:9 film frame with a clear focal point and depth (foreground, subject, background), painted full-bleed to all four edges (never paint black letterbox bars or a border: the game adds its own bars later and they cover the top tenth and the bottom fifth of the image, with the subtitles), so keep faces, hands and the key object inside the middle band. One single image: no panels, no split screen, no border, no frame, no captions, no subtitles, no speech bubbles, no watermark, no UI, unless the shot asks for it. No text or lettering anywhere unless the shot quotes it exactly.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
